label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Thanks Deirdre, I really appreciate you asking and giving me a chance to say how I feel, rather than just announcing the move.

I understand the numbers and that Bronwyn needs the extra help in Grade 00. I’m not asking for the move to be reversed, but I would be pretending if I said I wasn’t really sad about it. Noma has been with me in the Seahorses for three years, right from my first year teaching, and she’s taught me so much. She helped me find my feet with everything from sign-in sheets to the parent WhatsApp group, and she knows when a child needs something different. I still think about her sitting with Zayd under the jungle gym in Term 2 when nobody else could settle him.

I know she’ll only be across the courtyard, which does help, but not having her in our room will be a big adjustment. Those first weeks of Grade R are already emotional, with new children settling in and tears at the gate, so learning the routine with a new assistant at the same time feels quite daunting.

Could we please put two handover requests to SMT?
- Could Charlene come in for a day or two during 1–4 December, before her official start on 11 January, to spend time with Noma and see our routine?
- Could Noma join our morning ring for even 15 minutes each day in the first week back from 14 January? Her isiXhosa songs are such a familiar part of the Seahorses, and Luthando and Mia already know her from aftercare.

That overlap would mean a lot and help us start well together.
